pass_a_gloss: [Heading] Of the same holy Cyril, archbishop of Alexandria, a few fragments (ἀποσπάσματα) on the first epistle to the Corinthians (heading printed twice). [Lemma 1 Cor 1:1] Paul called (κλητός) apostle of Jesus Christ. The divine (θεσπέσιος) Paul says he has been sent (ἀπεστάλθαι) from Christ by good pleasure (εὐδοκίᾳ) of God and Father; this I think is 'through will (θελήματος) of God'; since through the Son is the willing (θέλειν) and working (ἐνεργεῖν) of the Father, through him again we say the saints have been appointed (προκεχειρῆσθαι) to apostleship. [Lemma] And Sosthenes the brother etc. That the power of the preachings (κηρυγμάτων) will benefit (ὀνήσει) not only Corinthians but all called in Christ to sanctification (ἁγιασμόν) through faith, he makes clear (διατρανοῖ) saying: sanctified in Christ in every place (ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ), theirs and ours. For the law (νόμος) did not command to do this in every place, but to come to the divine temple (νεών) itself in Jerusalem; for it feared, as likely, the easy-to-shift (εὐμετακόμιστον) of their mind, lest being commanded to worship (προσκυνεῖν) or sacrifice (θύειν) in every place they [have] the law as pretext (πρόφασιν) of change to worse things, and worship carved images (γλυπτοῖς), setting up for themselves temples and altars. But since we from the Gentiles (ἐθνῶν) have now been called through faith in Christ into kinship/belonging (οἰκειότητα) toward God, and have been enriched with security (ἀσφάλειαν) through the Holy Spirit, we are ordered to worship not all in Jerusalem but in every place; and this was what was said through the prophets: 'And they shall worship the Lord each from his place.' He writes then with Sosthenes to the church of God which Christ presented (παρέστησεν) to himself; and who was seen (ὦπτο) as it? All sanctified and called through Christ to justification (δικαίωσιν), calling upon (ἐπικαλούμενοι) his name in every place theirs and ours, that is, in the land of the Jews or in cities and countries of Gentiles. He proclaims Christ God by nature (κατὰ φύσιν), and with him and through him procures (πραγματεύεται) glory to God and Father; for he names the sanctified church of God, but again assigns (προσνέμει) them to Christ saying: 'If anyone has not the Spirit of Christ, this one is not his.' [Lemma 1 Cor 1:3] Grace to you and peace from God our Father and Lord Jesus Christ. He crowns with grace the believers, the grace from God and Father and Lord Jesus Christ; for through him and in him all things from God and Father; he is co-giver (συνδοτήρ) and co-supplier (συνχορηγός) with the begetter (γεγεννηκότι) of the good things from above, and distributor (διανομεύς) of the gifts (χαρισμάτων) from heaven, and he is the peace of all, making brilliant (καταλαμπρύνων) with grace from himself principalities, thrones and authorities and simply every rational (λογικήν) creation. [Lemma 1 Cor 1:10] But be perfected/knit (κατηρτισμένοι) in the same mind (νοΐ) and same judgment (γνώμῃ). That one must take dignity (κατασεμνύνεσθαι) in the Master's (δεσποτικῷ) name it was necessary and wise to persuade, he himself saying through one of the holy prophets: 'To those serving me shall be called a new name (ὄνομα καινόν) which shall be blessed on the earth'; for we are named Christians and are rich in the new name, of which some are justly deprived, departing from the right things (ὀρθῶν) of the Church, and attached to deceiving spirits (πνεύμασι πλάνοις) and the marvel-mongerings (τερατισμοῖς) of unholy false teachers (ψευδοδιδασκάλων), they have their [the teachers'] name, quite fittingly; for they are not of Christ, having taken shares (μερισάμενοι) in slander (δυσφημίαν) against him, split (κατεσχισμένοι) into different opinions (δόξας) and judgments, although Christ called his own in peace. And that he is one and not divided (μεμέρισται); one then we all are in Christ, and are knit for this in the same mind and judgment, he having bound us into one-soulness (ὁμοψυχίαν) by spiritual union (ἕνωσιν), the one saying about us to God and Father: 'I will that as I and you are one, so also they in [continues].'
pass_b_english: By the same holy Cyril, Archbishop of Alexandria: a few fragments on the First Epistle to the Corinthians.

“Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ” (1 Corinthians 1:1). The inspired Paul says that he has been sent by Christ, by the good pleasure of God the Father. For this, I think, is what “through the will of God” means (1 Corinthians 1:1). Since the Father’s willing and working are through the Son, we say that it is again through the Son that the saints have been appointed to their apostleship.

“And Sosthenes the brother,” and so on (1 Corinthians 1:1). Paul makes it plain that the power of the preaching will benefit not only the Corinthians but also all who have been called in Christ to the sanctification that comes through faith, when he says, “to those sanctified in Christ in every place, theirs and ours” (1 Corinthians 1:2). For the Law did not command this to be done in every place; it commanded them to come to the divine temple itself in Jerusalem (Deuteronomy 12:13–14). It feared, as one would expect, how easily their minds could be carried away: if they were commanded to worship or sacrifice in every place, they might perhaps take the Law as a pretext for turning to more shameful things, and worship carved images, setting up temples and altars for themselves.

But now that we who come from the Gentiles have been called, through faith in Christ, into a close bond with God, and have been enriched with the security that comes through the Holy Spirit, we are commanded to worship, not all of us in Jerusalem, but in every place. This, then, was what was spoken through the prophets: “And they shall worship the Lord, each one from his own place” (Zephaniah 2:11).

So he writes, together with Sosthenes, to the church of God, which Christ presented to himself (Ephesians 5:27). And who were seen to be that church? All who have been sanctified and called through Christ to justification, and who call upon his name “in every place, theirs and ours” (1 Corinthians 1:2), that is, whether in the land of the Jews or in the cities and countries of the Gentiles. He proclaims Christ to be God by nature, and with him and through him he renders glory to God the Father. For he names the sanctified “the church of God,” and yet he assigns them to Christ, saying, “If anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to him” (Romans 8:9).

“Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ” (1 Corinthians 1:3). He crowns those who have believed with the grace that comes from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. For through him and in him all things come from God the Father. He is co-giver and co-provider, with the one who begot him, of the good things from above, and he distributes the gifts from heaven. He himself is the peace of all (Ephesians 2:14), and by the grace that comes from himself he makes radiant principalities, thrones and authorities (Colossians 1:16), and, to put it simply, every rational creature.

“But be joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment” (1 Corinthians 1:10). It was both necessary and wise to persuade them that they ought to take their honor from the Master’s name, as the Master himself says through one of the holy prophets: “But those who serve me shall be called by a new name, which shall be blessed upon the earth” (Isaiah 65:15–16). For we have been named Christians, and we are rich in the new name. Some are rightly deprived of it: those who desert the right teaching of the Church and give themselves to deceiving spirits (1 Timothy 4:1) and to the wonder-mongering of certain unholy false teachers. They have taken those teachers’ name, and very fittingly, for they are not Christ’s. They have each taken a share in the blasphemy against him and have been split into differing opinions and judgments, although Christ called his own in peace.

It was needful also to persuade them that Christ himself is one and is not divided (1 Corinthians 1:13). So we are all one in Christ (Galatians 3:28), and for this we have been joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment, since he has bound us into one soul by a spiritual union, he who says of us to God the Father, “I desire that, as I and you are one, so they too in […]” (John 17:21–22).

Sosthenes is 'the brother' (ὁ ἀδελφός), not 'our brother'; ἁγιασμός kept as 'sanctification' to match 'sanctified' in the quoted verse; αἰσχίω is 'more shameful', not just 'worse'; λέγων αὐτός makes the Master (the Lord) the speaker through the prophet, which 'he himself' left unclear; καὶ ὅτι εἷς ἔστιν αὐτός still depends on ἀναγκαῖον ἦν ... ἀναπεῖσαι (it was necessary to persuade them that Christ is one), not a free-standing statement.
